title: ESP32-DevKitC
notes: GPIO6-11 (D2, D3, CMD on J2-16..18; D1, D0, CLK on J3-17..19) are wired to the module's SPI flash: they are on the headers, but do not use them.

GPIO16/17 are usable only on boards with ESP32-WROOM and ESP32-SOLO-1 modules; ESP32-WROVER boards reserve them. The pin rule esp32.psram_16_17 blocks them for the module variant WROVER-E (PSRAM), leaves them free for WROOM-32E and marks them caution while the variant is unknown.
VP (GPIO36), VN (GPIO39), IO34 and IO35 are input only; GPIO37/38 are not broken out.
Strapping pins on the headers: GPIO0 (Boot button), GPIO2, GPIO5, GPIO12 (MTDI), GPIO15 (MTDO).
With Wi-Fi on, the ADC2 pins (GPIO0, 2, 4, 12-15, 25-27) cannot be used for ADC; ADC1 is on VP, VN and IO32-IO35.
TX/RX (GPIO1/GPIO3) are U0TXD/U0RXD, used for flashing and the console over the USB-to-UART bridge.
Earlier V4 boards: C15 may make the board boot into Download mode or disturb a clock output on GPIO0; remove C15 if that happens.

Standard module: ESP32-WROOM-32E (ESP32-DevKitC-32E: 4 MB flash, no PSRAM; module variant WROOM-32E). The ordering table also lists ESP32-DevKitC-32UE (ESP32-WROOM-32UE) and ESP32-DevKitC-VE/-VIE (ESP32-WROVER-E/-IE with 8 MB PSRAM); set the module variant WROVER-E for the latter.
The user guide text does not name the USB-to-UART bridge chip; its pin layout figure shows a chip marked CP2102 (read from the figure, unverified).

Download button. Holding down **Boot** and then pressing **EN** initiates Firmware Download mode for downloading firmware through the serial port.

citations.quote: TXD & RXD are usually used for flashing and debugging
The pins D0, D1, D2, D3, CMD and CLK are used internally for communication between ESP32 and SPI flash memory.
Avoid using these pins, as it may disrupt access to the SPI flash memory/SPI RAM.
The pins GPIO16 and GPIO17 are available for use only on the boards with the modules ESP32-WROOM and ESP32-SOLO-1. The boards with ESP32-WROVER modules have the pins reserved for internal use.
GPIO6-11 and GPIO16-17 are usually connected to the SPI flash and PSRAM integrated on the module and therefore should not be used for other purposes
GPIO34-39 can only be set as input mode
GPIO0, GPIO2, GPIO5, GPIO12 (MTDI), and GPIO15 (MTDO) are strapping pins
ADC2 pins cannot be used when Wi-Fi is used
TXD & RXD are usually used for flashing and debugging
The component C15 may cause the following issues on earlier ESP32-DevKitC V4 boards:
* The board may boot into Download mode
* If you output clock on GPIO0, C15 may impact the signal
In case these issues occur, please remove the component.
Single USB-to-UART bridge chip, providing transfer rates up to 3 Mbps.
